item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I once saw a clip where Teller (from the Penn & Teller magic duo) was being shown the classic cups and ball slight of hand by a master street performer in India. The performer knew that Teller knew how the trick was done, and so he did it very lazily and it was very obvious when he palmed the ball and which cup he slipped it under. Teller, playing the good rube, went ahaed and picked the cup he was supposed to as if he hadn't spotted the bad palm-job. But, that's where the ball was. The performer mimed the bad palming without actually moving the ball, and did it so well that a profesional magician not 6 inches away fell for the anti-trick.

You have done the same thing here. We all know how the Foundation-verse works. This re-assembly cult must be Broken God, it's just obvious, and we wait for the twist. But, like the street performer did to Teller, you've just let us trick ourselves. So when the inevitable conclusion plays out, it's straight-forward and obvious, and utterly shocking. Like a last step that isn't there. Literary judo, letting the reader do all the heavy lifting. it's what M. Night Shyamalan wishes he could do.

item.content:encoded:
This is technically not the first thing I posted to the site. It is my first tale though. Technically not the first one I started writing, but it is the first one I was happy enough to post. I am working on a longer-form narrative in the Bellerverse as well.

During my first week I violated that "don't try to rush to contribute something" piece of advice and submitted a mediocre SCP article that made it to about -7 before I took it down. It lurks in my sandbox, waiting for me to go back and rewrite it.

Anyway, I'm really psyched by all the positive feedback! Thanks everyone! I'm looking forward to contributing what I can to the site.
